label: NBHA Barrel Racing
source: National Barrel Horse Association 2026 Season Official Rulebook

docs.title: Mission, Vision, and Core Values
docs.text: The National Barrel Horse Association's mission is to promote and expand the sport of barrel racing, utilizing a divisional format, which allows a diverse membership to compete on any breed of equine. The vision of NBHA is to be the leading association for barrel racing worldwide. NBHA values passion, integrity, diversity, innovation, and a commitment to our members. The goal of NBHA is to increase the number of participants, improve the quality of shows and enhance the sport of barrel racing. NBHA supports the expansion of events by providing director support at the local, state, and regional level.

docs.title: Introduction and Interpretation of Rules
docs.text: Official NBHA rules address the needs of NBHA members, promote fairness, eliminate confusion, and assist show organizers in the production of an event that reflects the standards. These Rules cannot cover all possible situations that may arise during a show, nor can they regulate all administrative questions. Where cases are not precisely regulated by a Rule, it should be possible to reach a reasonable decision by looking at the Rule book and the Director's Handbook. The Rules assume that NBHA Directors, Show Management and Headquarter staff have the necessary competence, sound judgment and absolute objectivity. Too detailed a rule might deprive the official of his/her freedom of judgment and thus prevent him/her from finding the solution to a problem dictated by fairness, logic, and special factors. The rulebook is organised into Section A: Competition Rules; Section B: Show Sanctioning; Section C: Earned Points; Section D: Payout; Section E: Rules Related to State, Super and World Shows; Section F: Penalties and/or Disqualifications; Section G: Dress Code; Section H: Protests & Complaints; Section I: NBHA Intellectual Property.

docs.title: Barrel race definition and barrel specifications
docs.text: An NBHA barrel race is an electronically timed event using three identical barrels set in a cloverleaf pattern. Barrels may not be weighted (i.e., sand or water). Barrels must be metal or plastic and must be enclosed on both ends.

docs.title: Starting gate
docs.text: The starting gate or gates must remain the same throughout the entire event. If more than one start gate is available, it must be offered or denied to all riders equally regardless of the direction they run.

docs.title: Start/finish line and barrel positions
docs.text: The start/finish line and the barrel positions should be permanently marked and must remain the same throughout the entire event.

docs.title: Pattern minimum distances
docs.text: The pattern at an NBHA show must meet the following conditions: (a) The first two barrels must be a minimum of 15 feet off the side fence. (b) A minimum of 30 feet between the third barrel and the back fence. (c) A minimum of 30 feet between the timeline and the first barrel.

docs.title: Ground conditions and drag intervals
docs.text: The ground conditions within the arena must remain consistent throughout the event. The ground around the barrels must be reworked and leveled after no more than each 5 contestants have competed. Drag intervals must be consistent. Example: After every 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 draw numbers. If scratches exist, the drag must still remain in the same position.

docs.title: Method of working the ground
docs.text: The preferred method of working the ground is with a ground tool pulled by some type of motor vehicle. Hand raking is not acceptable.

docs.title: Crossing the starting line constitutes a run
docs.text: Any time a contestant crosses the starting line, time will begin, and this will constitute an attempt at a run.

docs.title: Western saddle required; no bareback
docs.text: Contestants must compete using a western saddle. Riding bareback in a sanctioned NBHA class will result in a disqualification. Additionally, no bareback riding is permitted at any Super Show or World Championship Show at any time and can result in a fine or further action for repeat offenses.

docs.title: No time: off pattern
docs.text: A contestant will be given a 'no time' for going off pattern.

docs.title: No time: knocking over a barrel
docs.text: A contestant will be given a 'no time' for knocking over a barrel completely, regardless of if it stands back up on either end. Touching the barrel is permitted, without penalty.

docs.title: No time: running out of turn or wrong horse
docs.text: A contestant will be given a 'no time' for running out of turn and/or riding a horse other than the horse in the drawn position. It is the contestant's responsibility to know their drawn position. In the case where the announcer clearly announces the wrong running order and can identify their mistake, a contestant shall keep their time. At the completion of the 'out-of-order' run, the ground shall be drug for those riders remaining in the drag, if any.

docs.title: No time: rider falls off
docs.text: A contestant will be given a 'no time' if the rider falls off after crossing the starting timer. A rider who falls off a horse completely, before the starting line, regardless if the horse breaks the timer, a re-run will be offered in that moment in the same draw position, and not at a later time.

docs.title: Barrel or timer moved off marker; altered pattern
docs.text: If a barrel or timer is moved off its marker during competition, they must be reset prior to the next competitor's run to the proper markers and all contestants who competed on the incorrect pattern must re-run, or else a no-time will be given. If the pattern is altered in any way during the running of a class, such that it cannot be restored to its original layout, all runs made to that point are void for the purpose of NBHA points. NBHA points may be awarded only if the entire class is rerun. An altered pattern includes but is not limited to: changes in the staked position of the barrels; a change in the position of the timing device, either vertically or horizontally; or a change in the position of the entry gate(s).

docs.title: Show stopped by weather or other circumstances
docs.text: Should weather or other circumstances prevent a show from proceeding once it has begun, points from any class not fully completed cannot be awarded to any rider.

docs.title: Riding multiple horses; horse shown by more than one person
docs.text: Contestants may ride any horse, regardless of ownership, and may ride as many horses as they choose in a class unless otherwise approved by the NBHA Headquarters. However, a horse may not be shown by more than one person in a class, unless the following conditions are met: (a) Both contestants are members of the same immediate family who also reside in the same household (husband, wife, siblings, children, and grandchildren). Children and grandchildren who are attending school away from home, but who reside part of the year with their parents or grandparents are included under this rule. (b) Neither contestant is showing any other horse in that class. (c) In no case will the same horse be run more than twice in the same class.

docs.title: Entries close
docs.text: Entries for an NBHA class will close when the first horse in that class runs, unless otherwise stated on District communications.

docs.title: The draw
docs.text: At all NBHA sanctioned shows, the draw shall be done in a random manner (computer, shuffling cards, drawing numbered chips, etc.). All horses in the draw must be named using registered names, when available. Riders with multiple entries must ride their horses in the position in which they draw up. Once set, the draw may not be changed, except to accommodate entries with the same horse or rider, or entries involving members of the same immediate family, as defined in Section A, Rule 11a, which have drawn up close to each other. What constitutes 'close to each other' will be determined by Show Management; however, a consistent standard should be adhered to for the class. The draw may not be changed to give preference to any rider or to accommodate another commitment of a particular rider such as work or another barrel race. Changes must be moved to the end.

docs.title: Combining classes into one draw
docs.text: Combining classes into one draw is permitted. This must be stated on show information. Any abuse of this can result in restriction of future use at the National Office's discretion.

docs.title: One horse in the arena
docs.text: Only one horse may be in the competition arena at any time during competition.

docs.title: Reruns for timer failure or misplaced barrels
docs.text: Reruns shall be granted if the official and any available back up electronic timers fails to work properly or if the barrels are not placed properly on their markers. Any penalty incurred on the original run shall not be applied against the rerun; however, any penalty occurring on the rerun shall result in a no time.

docs.title: Completing the pattern after a no-time; training in the arena
docs.text: Contestants who are given a no-time, either for missing the pattern or knocking down a barrel, may complete the pattern. However, show management may, at its discretion, ask a rider who is taking excessive time to train to leave the arena immediately. If such request is not complied with, a $25 fine may be assessed, payable to the district awards fund.

docs.title: Two-minute rule for difficult horses
docs.text: NBHA Officials have the right to disqualify any uncontrolled, refusing or likewise difficult horse which does not begin the pattern within two minutes of the time the rider has been called. This rule does not apply to competitors who have not checked in with gate personnel.

docs.title: Stallions and uncontrollable horses
docs.text: It is highly recommended that stallions be ground handled solely by individuals 18 and over. There is zero tolerance for uncontrollable, dangerous horses whether stallion or not. Any negligent behavior resulting in improper control of any horse can be grounds for disqualification.

docs.title: Sanctioning request and fee
docs.text: For a show to be sanctioned by the NBHA, an official request must be made to the District Director on an NBHA Sanctioned Show Request Form. A $30 sanctioning fee must accompany this request. If the show is to be published in Barrel Horse News, the request form must be received by NBHA Headquarters 60 days prior to the show. To be approved as a sanctioned show, the request form and fee must be received at NBHA Headquarters at least 14 days prior to the requested show date. State Directors will have final approval for all sanctioned shows. NBHA points will not be awarded for shows that are not properly sanctioned.

docs.title: Payout formats
docs.text: Sanctioned shows may pay out on either the 3D, 4D, or 5D format.

docs.title: One show per date per district
docs.text: The NBHA will sanction only one show on a given date within a district, except that two separate NBHA runs may be sanctioned on the same day at the same arena.

docs.title: Date conflicts with championships and Tour Shows
docs.text: No sanctioned NBHA point shows within the continental United States will be approved for dates that would interfere with members from attending their State Championships, the World Championships, the Youth World Championships. No sanctioned NBHA point shows within the continental United States will be approved within 350 miles of a Tour Show regardless of region. Exceptions may be permitted with timely approval from the NBHA Headquarters.

docs.title: First-come, first-serve sanctioning
docs.text: Shows will be sanctioned on a first-come, first-serve basis. The NBHA reserves the right to refuse sanctioning for a particular date or show if it is determined not to be in the best interest of the NBHA or its members.

docs.title: Number of shows per district
docs.text: A district shall have no fewer than six (6) nor more than eighteen (18) sanctioned shows per competition season.

docs.title: Open to all members; no forced entries or fees
docs.text: To be sanctioned, a show must offer all NBHA members in good standing, regardless of age or sex, the opportunity to compete. NBHA members may not be required to enter any other class, or join any other association or club. Competitors must not be required to pay any non-member fee or permit fee greater than $3 to any association or club not officially affiliated with NBHA, as a condition of riding in an NBHA sanctioned class.

docs.title: Classes of competition (age categories)
docs.text: There will be four classes of competition as follows: Open (all ages); Youth (12 years of age and under as of January 1st of the competition year); Teen (13-18 years of age and under as of January 1st of the competition year); Senior (50 years of age and over as of the date of the show). Proof of age may be required at the discretion of Show Management. A Youth competitor may not rollup to a Teen division for any reason.

docs.title: Rollover/carryover of times between classes
docs.text: Show Management may allow eligible contestants to rollover/carryover their times from one class to another so long as the classes take place on the same day and pattern and arena/drag specifics are identical. Contestants wishing to rollover a time must declare their intent before event begins, unless otherwise stated as prior to rider's draw position, but never after the contestant has competed. Any contestant carrying time must pay the applicable entry fee for both classes and is eligible to win prize money and NBHA points just as if the time was run in the other class. The pattern for the Open, Youth, Teen and Senior must be exactly the same and must not be changed in any manner.

docs.title: Points and payout only among qualifying riders
docs.text: The NBHA points, and payout, if any, will be determined based only on those riders who qualify for that particular class (Youth, Teen or Seniors).

docs.title: Combined Youth and Teen class
docs.text: The Director has the option to run one class, usually called 'Youth', and combine the Youth and Teen categories into one draw, and one payout, however the points must be calculated separately according to the points guidelines.

docs.title: Electronic timing required
docs.text: All sanctioned shows must have an electronic timing system and conform to the NBHA rules. NBHA events will be timed to thousandths of seconds if the clock being used displays three decimal places.

docs.title: Submitting results and posting point standings
docs.text: The District Director must submit show results of all NBHA classes (Open, Youth, Teen and Senior) to their State Director within seven days after the show. Results must be reported in the 5-D format, regardless of whether the show used the 3-D, 4-D or 5-D payout formula. Point standings must be posted in a public location by the District Director at every show or on a public website for members to see. When a member disagrees with points awarded, that member will have 14 days, from the date points are posted, to bring any discrepancies to the attention of the District Director and, if necessary, to file a written protest in accordance with Section H of this Rule Book. If points are not posted in a public location at a show, members should notify their State Director. If that fails to resolve the problem, the member may notify their Regional Director in writing.

docs.title: Travel distance hardship; co-sanction approval
docs.text: Directors must use good judgment in order not to create a travel distance hardship on members and risk revocation of sanction. State Directors will have final approval authority for all co-sanctioned shows.

docs.title: Co-sanctioned show fee
docs.text: The sanction fee for a co-sanctioned show is $30 from each district participating, no matter how many districts participate. Each district must submit their own form. A co-sanctioned show must be sanctioned for the district in which it takes place unless specific permission has been given by the District Director.

docs.title: Host district cancels co-sanction
docs.text: If a show is co-sanctioned, and the host district later decides to cancel the sanction, the show may continue as sanctioned for any or all the visiting districts which decide to keep the sanction. The original host district may not sanction another show within that district on the same day.

docs.title: Membership card not required at entry
docs.text: A contestant's current NBHA membership card or a copy of current membership application is no longer required to the show secretary prior to entering an NBHA sanctioned show.

docs.title: Non-member permit fee
docs.text: Non-members may compete for prize money at an NBHA sanctioned show only upon payment of a non-member permit fee. A non-member permit fee, in the amount of up to ten dollars ($10.00) will be collected from each non-member seeking to enter each NBHA sanctioned show. The fee collected will permit non-members to enter one NBHA show and compete in all classes for which they are qualified. Non-member permit fees collected will be deposited in the district account for year-end awards. District Directors may waive the non-member fee uniformly per event if they so choose. The NBHA reserves the right to refuse co-sanctioning for a particular date or show if it is determined not to be in the best interest of the NBHA or its members.

docs.title: NBHA logo in show advertising
docs.text: Organizations and individuals requesting NBHA sanctioned shows must use the official NBHA logo in all show bills and displayed advertising. Classified advertising and show listings must contain the words 'NBHA Sanctioned.' Camera-ready copies of the NBHA logo are available on the NBHA website or by contacting the National Headquarters.

docs.title: Sponsor promotional items
docs.text: As a condition of sanction, shows may be asked to display promotional items provided by select NBHA national sponsors.

docs.title: Membership in good standing; renewal and grace period
docs.text: To earn and maintain points, a competitor must be a member in good standing of the NBHA. Members who fail to renew their membership within 30 days of their expiration date will forfeit any accumulated points previously earned during the competition year, however race count for State Show qualifications purposes will remain. NBHA policy allows for a 30-day administrative grace period beyond the expiration date before the membership is officially marked as lapsed. Members who are in their administrative grace period should therefore not be credited with NBHA points unless they renew online before competing. Members past the expiration date are also liable for non-member permit fees. Members may not use the administrative grace period to compete in shows restricted to members, such as NBHA State Championships, Super Shows, National Championship Series, or World Championships.

docs.title: Points in one district only
docs.text: NBHA members may accumulate points in only one district at a time during the competition year. Members are responsible for designating their district online at the time of joining or renewing. Members lose accumulated points in a district when they designate and start competing for NBHA points in another district during the competition year.

docs.title: Lead line competitors receive no points
docs.text: At no time will a lead line competitor receive points toward World Championship qualifications.

docs.title: Division time brackets
docs.text: Divisions for points are determined by time brackets. The fastest time in the class will set the time for payback and District 00 points. Whatever district or districts sanction the show their district members' fastest time will set the time for their district points. If sanctioned by more than one district each district's fastest time will set their time for their district points. 1st Division: fastest time in the class and those who place in this division. 2nd Division: fastest time in the class plus one-half second and those who place in this division. 3rd Division: fastest time in the class plus one second and those who place in this division. 4th Division: fastest time in the class plus one and one-half seconds and those who place in this division. 5th Division: fastest time in the class plus two seconds and those who place in this division. Note: The 5th division is not limited to a one-half second interval from two to two and one-half seconds off the fastest time. However, riders must make a good faith effort to run the pattern as fast as their ability will allow.

docs.title: Points scale and ties
docs.text: NBHA points will be awarded in all classes and divisions on a 5,4,3,2,1 basis for 1st place through 5th place among NBHA members in that competition district only, regardless of the number of entries or paying places. If two or more riders tie, the points for the tied positions should be added together and divided equally among the riders who tied. If non-members place among the top points positions, the points skip those riders and continue to the riders below them who are active within the district.

docs.title: Points in combined Youth/Teen class
docs.text: The Director has the option to run one class combining the Youth and Teen, usually called 'Youth' collectively into one draw and one payout, however the points must be calculated separately at the individual show level. Therefore, you will have a fastest Youth time receiving 5 Youth 1D points and a fastest Teen time receiving 5 Teen 1D points, and those two times will ultimately set the brackets from the subsequent points and divisions.

docs.title: Purpose of NBHA points and district awards
docs.text: NBHA points are strictly for qualifications to World Championship shows. Districts may have different qualifications and sets of points used for district awards, such as volunteer standards or fundraising. This shall be determined by the State and District Directors. District awards are not required, but highly recommended.

docs.title: Example of time brackets for points
Fewer than five horses in a division
docs.text: Should fewer than five horses place in a division, NBHA points will be awarded beginning with five points for 1st place as usual, and extra points not earned are never redistributed.

docs.title: No points for knocked barrel
docs.text: NBHA points will not be awarded for any run during which a contestant knocks over a barrel.

docs.title: Entering more than one class
docs.text: Competitors may enter more than one class. For example, competitors in the Youth 5D or Senior 5D classes may also qualify in the Open 5D class.

docs.title: Points with multiple horses
docs.text: Competitors may ride as many horses as they wish in each class. However, the competitor with multiple entries will receive points only for the highest placing horse in each division per class.

docs.title: Points at co-sanctioned shows
docs.text: At a co-sanctioned show, each district's members are given their points separately. That is, the highest placing 1D rider from each district gets 5 points, and so on.

docs.title: One World Championship qualification per division
docs.text: A competitor may qualify only one entry for the NBHA World Championships in each of the Open 5D divisions, the Youth 5D divisions, or the Senior 5D divisions, based on accumulated points.

docs.title: Points awarded to the rider
docs.text: NBHA points, in all classes and divisions are awarded to the rider.

docs.title: Horse entries at World Championships and National Championship Series
docs.text: A horse may be entered only once in each class at the NBHA World Championships and National Championship Series, with the exception of immediate family members, as defined in Section A Paragraph 9 above, who qualify in the same class. In no case will the same horse be entered more than twice in the same class. (Note: immediate family is defined in Section A, Rule 11a.)

docs.title: District World Show qualifiers and ties
docs.text: Each district may qualify for the world show ten (10) total riders in each division of each class (Open, Youth, Teen, and Senior) unless applicable ties cross over the 10th place position. Ties consume the number of places that there are competitors, for example, a two-way tie with 6 points each for 3rd place then consumes the 3rd and 4th place collectively. In this case, someone with 5 points is considered 5th. If at any time a tie consumes 10th or better then all individuals in that group are to be turned into NBHA as qualifiers.

docs.title: Roving district 00: definition
docs.text: The roving district is designated '00'. It works like a geographical district except that members may earn points at any show which is sanctioned for any district in their state. This has been developed to provide another option for members who want a greater selection in the number of shows they attend, or who have work or other obligations which make it difficult to commit to the schedule of a particular district.

docs.title: Roving district 00: setup and ten-show limit
docs.text: It is up to the discretion of the State Director whether to initiate the '00' district within a state. A District Director must be appointed to keep the points for the '00' district. This could be either the State Director or an appointed District Director. '00' members may count up to ten shows per class toward their year end point totals. The '00' Director will be responsible for submitting the year-end report with World Show qualifiers to Headquarters.

docs.title: Roving district 00: declaring
docs.text: Members declare the '00' district just like any other. A member may not declare '00', and a regular district at the same time.

docs.title: Roving district 00: indicating a show counts
docs.text: A '00' member who competes in an NBHA sanctioned show must indicate on the entry card or form, before the competition, whether they will count this show for points. If the member receives no points, the show still counts toward the allotment of shows.

docs.title: Roving district 00: time splits
docs.text: Time splits for the '00' district will be taken off the fastest time in the class, regardless of whether that time is posted by a member or non-member, or which district the rider is a member of.

docs.title: Jackpot percentage and office charge
docs.text: The required payoff for NBHA sanctioned shows: a minimum of 75% of all entry fees must go to the jackpot. Exception: if a show offers at least $1,000 added money on a combined level of the sanctioned NBHA classes alone, not combined double races if held in the same day, a minimum of 70% of all entry fees must go to the jackpot. That is, a maximum of 25% (or a maximum of 30% if at least $1,000 added) may be withheld as the 'office charge.' If more than 25% is withheld pursuant to the above, this fact must be stated on any show bills or flyers. This is exclusive of other fees which may be charged for specific purposes such as State District Awards Fees, timer fee, processing fee or arena fee. While such charges are permitted, they must not be excessive, must be clearly stated in all advertising and show bills, and must be directed to the specific purposes as labeled; for example, the timer fees must either be paid to the timer owner/operator, or put toward the purchase of a timer for the district. The charging of a 'processing fee' to district shows, the sole purpose of which is to add to the general revenue of the show, is not permitted.

docs.title: Awards fee
docs.text: To help support the State Championships by raising money for State Awards all NBHA sanctioned shows must charge a minimum $2.00 awards fee with a minimum $1.00 going to the District and a minimum $1.00 going to the State Director for State Championships. If your district will not be awarding year-end awards there may not be a district fee. Each State can elect for higher fees for State and District if approved by the Regional Directors.

docs.title: Payout format time splits
docs.text: Shows may choose to payout their classes in a 3D, 4D or 5D although points are always awarded in a 5D. The time splits between the divisions for a 3D payout class is 1.0 - 1.0 second splits, 4D payout class may be either 0.5 - 0.5 - 0.5 second splits or 0.5 - 0.5 - 1 second splits, and splits for a 5D format must be 0.5 second between all divisions. It is up to the Director to choose the payout best suited.

docs.title: Division share of jackpot
docs.text: In a payout, the total jackpotted entry fees are to be divided into divisions as follows. Original Option: 3D: D1 50%, D2 30%, D3 20%. 4D: D1 35%, D2 30%, D3 20%, D4 15%. 5D: D1 30%, D2 25%, D3 20%, D4 15%, D5 10%. Optional B: 3D: not available. 4D: D1 32%, D2 28%, D3 22%, D4 18%. 5D: D1 26%, D2 23%, D3 20%, D4 17%, D5 14%.

docs.title: Added money division
docs.text: Added money will be divided in the same ratio used above for the entry fees or split evenly among all divisions.

docs.title: Apportioning added money among classes
docs.text: There are no restrictions regarding how added money is apportioned among classes at a show. For example, a show may add money to the Open but not to Youth or Seniors.

docs.title: Minimum places paid
docs.text: The payout tables (D.7 3-D, 4-D and 5-D Format) show the minimum number of places to be paid for the stated number of entries, and the percentage of the division's money paid to each place. You may use the standard or Option B (Alt. Option) selection to determine how many places to pay. For payout percentages when desiring to payout more than 12 places, contact the NBHA Headquarters.

docs.title: 5-D Format places paid table
docs.text: 5-D Format, percentage per place by number of entries, columns as printed (Standard / Alt. Option; '-' means no value printed). Standard - / Alt 1-25: 1st 100%. Standard 1-20 / Alt 26-50: 60%, 40%. Standard 21-40 / Alt 51-100: 50%, 30%, 20%. Standard 41-80 / Alt 101-143: 40%, 30%, 20%, 10%. Standard 81-150 / Alt 144-200: 30%, 25%, 20%, 15%, 10%. Standard 151-200 / Alt 201-250: 28%, 22%, 18%, 14%, 10%, 8%. Standard - / Alt 251-300: 26%, 20%, 15%, 12%, 10%, 9%, 8%. Standard 201+ / Alt 251-300: 24%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 10%, 8%, 7%, 6%. Standard - / Alt 301-350: 22%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 10%, 8%, 6%, 5%, 4%. Standard - / Alt 351-400: 20%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 9.5%, 7.5%, 6%, 5%, 4%, 3%. Standard - / Alt 401-450: 19%, 17%, 14.5%, 12%, 9.5%, 7%, 6%, 5%, 4%, 3.5%, 2.5%. Standard - / Alt 451+: 19%, 17%, 14%, 11%, 9%, 7%, 5.5%, 5%, 4%, 3.5%, 2.75%, 2.25% (12 places). For payout percentages when desiring to payout more than 12 places, contact the NBHA Headquarters.

docs.title: Director checks payback
docs.text: District Directors will check payback in all NBHA classes. Paying more than the stated places requires approval of the District Director.

docs.title: Prize money paid on-site
docs.text: All prize money must be paid out on-site at the conclusion of the event unless otherwise advertised and pre-approved by the National Office. In the event that circumstances arise preventing accurate payout on show day, the Director must remit all payments to riders within two weeks of the show, as well as notify the National Office of the issue on the next business day.

docs.title: No prize money for knocked barrel
docs.text: Prize money will NOT be paid to any contestant who knocks over a barrel.

docs.title: Unclaimed division money
docs.text: At any NBHA show, if not enough riders qualify in a division as monies to be paid, the money which is unaccounted for shall be divided equally among those who have placed in that division, or based upon the percentages of payout for the placings as shown in the payout charts until no leftover money remains. If no riders qualify in a division, the prize money for that division shall be divided among those riders in the other divisions of that class who have won prize money.

docs.title: Payouts on posted results
docs.text: Payouts must be included on the results posted after a race.

docs.title: Show Manager rulings at State, Super and World Shows
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: All rulings made in accordance to the rule book and for instances not referenced in the rule book, will be made by the Show Manager and will be considered final.

docs.title: State Shows: general rules apply
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: State Shows: All NBHA rules will apply as set forth in the rulebook if not addressed in the State Show rules.

docs.title: State Shows: membership
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: All participants in State Championships must be current members in good standing at the time of show.

docs.title: State Shows: no district points
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: State Shows may not be used for District show points or qualifications of any kind.

docs.title: State Shows: one per year
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: No member may compete in more than one NBHA State Championship during a calendar year.

docs.title: State Shows: three-show eligibility
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: To be eligible to enter a State Championship in any class all participants must have competed in three separate district shows in at least one sanctioned class in the declared competition district during the time between State Shows.

docs.title: State Shows: no buy-in
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: Under no circumstance shall a State offer a buy-in option to State Finals. Members must compete to obtain qualifications. No qualification will be given for riders who do not compete.

docs.title: State Shows: draw positions fixed
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At State Shows, horse and rider combinations may not change draw positions under any circumstance.

docs.title: State Shows: no rider substitutions
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At State Shows, no rider substitutions allowed.

docs.title: State Shows: horse changes
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At State Shows, horse changes must be received in the show office prior to your competition run. When a Short Go/Finals is involved, members must compete on the horse they qualified on.

docs.title: State Shows: timer malfunction rerun
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At State Shows, electric timers must be used for all rides. Should the timer malfunction a rerun will be granted immediately after the event is completed for the day and after a drag, or at the discretion of the Show Manager.

docs.title: State Shows: tie for a State title (run-off)
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: In the event of a tie for a State title in any Division (1st Place only in any D), a run-off will occur using the following protocol: (i) A Show Official will toss a coin to determine running order, unless all tied parties mutually agree to a coin toss to determine the clear winner without a runoff. (ii) In the event of a run-off, each contestant will be given a minimum of 30 minutes of rest before having to ride in a runoff. (iii) During the runoff, any barrels knocked down will result in a 5 second penalty per barrel down. (iv) Winning monies related to a tie will be split 50/50 or evenly in the case of more than two individuals in a tie and contestants will be deemed Co-Champions. Prizes will be awarded to the results from the runoff or the mutually agreed upon flip. (v) If a contestant fails to contact the Show Official within 30 minutes of announced results, he or she will forfeit the opportunity of flipping a coin or running for first choice of awards. This will not impact the event payoff, or the contestants being considered Co-Champions. (vi) It is the contestant's responsibility to seek show results.

docs.title: State Shows: ties not related to a State title
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: In the event of a tie not related to a State title, in which awards are given: (i) A coin flip will be used to determine who will receive first choice of awards. If a contestant fails to contact the Show Official within 30 minutes of announced results, he or she will forfeit the opportunity of flipping a coin for first choice of awards. (ii) Winning monies related to a tie will be split 50/50 or evenly in the case of more than two individuals in a tie.

docs.title: Super Shows: general rules apply
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: Super Shows: All NBHA rules will apply as set forth in the rulebook if not addressed in the Super Show rules.

docs.title: Super Shows: membership
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: It is recommended that all participants in Super Shows be a current member in good standing, however NBHA reserves the right to open Super Shows to all competitors. If awards are given, only current members would be eligible for such awards.

docs.title: Super Shows: lead line
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: Lead line in a NBHA Super Show class will result in a no-time.

docs.title: Super Shows: entries
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At Super Shows, entries may remain open beyond the start of the classes. Entries will close at the advertised times.

docs.title: Super Shows: draw positions fixed
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At Super Shows, horse and rider combinations may not change draw positions under any circumstance.

docs.title: Super Shows: carryovers
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At Super Shows, carryover classes may exist on separate days if deemed necessary.

docs.title: Super Shows: payouts
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At Super Shows, payouts per division will follow the percentages as stated in Section D, Rule 2. The percentages and number of placings within each D will be determined based on added money, number of entries and entry fee, and at the discretion of the Show Manager and may differ from Section D, Rule 2.

docs.title: Super Shows: check-in and three-call
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At Super Shows, riders must check in with the gate help during the time the tractors are dragging for their set of runners. Failure to check in will result in a three-call for the rider and the rider missing their run if not able to enter the arena during those three calls.

docs.title: Super Shows: ties
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At Super Shows, in the event of a tie where awards are applicable, a coin toss will be used to determine who will receive preference of/or any awards, but prize money will be evenly split.

docs.title: World Shows: general rules apply
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: World Shows: All NBHA rules will apply as set forth in the rulebook if not addressed in the World Show rules.

docs.title: World Shows: membership
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: All participants in World Shows must be current members in good standing.

docs.title: World Shows: draw positions fixed
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At World Shows, horse and rider combinations may not change draw positions under any circumstance.

docs.title: World Shows: no rider substitutions
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At World Shows, no rider substitutions allowed.

docs.title: World Shows: lead line
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: Lead line in a Championship class will result in a no-time.

docs.title: World Shows: check-in and three-call
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At World Shows, riders must check in with the gate help during the time the tractors are dragging for their set of runners. Failure to check in will result in a three-call for the rider and the rider missing their run if not able to enter the arena during those three calls.

docs.title: World Shows: carryovers
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At World Shows, carryover classes may exist on separate days if deemed necessary.

docs.title: World Shows: payouts
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: At World Shows, payouts per division will follow the percentages as stated in Section D, Rule 2. The percentages and number of placings within each D will be determined based on added money, number of entries and entry fee, and at the discretion of the Show Manager.

docs.title: World Shows: tie for a World Championship title (run-off)
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: In the event of a tie for a World Championship title in any Division (1st Place only in any D), a run-off will occur for awards using the following protocol, however riders will be considered Co-Champions: (i) A Show Official will toss a coin to determine running order, unless all tied parties mutually agree to a coin toss to determine the rider who gets first choice of awards without a runoff. (ii) In the event of a run-off, each contestant will be given a minimum of 30 minutes of rest before having to ride in a runoff. (iii) During the runoff, any barrels knocked down will result in a 5 second penalty per barrel down. (iv) Winning monies related to a tie will be split 50/50 or evenly in the case of more than two individuals in a tie and contestants will be deemed Co-Champions. Prizes will be awarded to the results from the runoff or the mutually agreed upon flip. (v) If a contestant fails to contact the Show Official within 30 minutes of announced results, he or she will forfeit the opportunity of flipping a coin or running for first choice of awards. This will not impact the event payoff, or the contestants being considered Co-Champions. (vi) It is the contestant's responsibility to seek show results.

docs.title: World Shows: ties not related to a title
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: In the event of a tie not related to a World Championship title, in which awards are given: (i) A coin flip will be used to determine who will receive first choice of awards. If a contestant fails to contact the Show Official within 30 minutes of announced results, he or she will forfeit the opportunity of flipping a coin for first choice of awards. (ii) Winning monies related to a tie will be split 50/50 or evenly in the case of more than two individuals in a tie.

docs.title: Wildcards
docs.section: E. State, Super and World Shows
docs.text: (i) Wildcards are good for one World Championship qualification. One Wildcard = One horse qualification into one Championship class. (ii) They cannot be replaced if physically lost. (iii) These do not expire and they are transferable with proper transfer form. NBHA does not sell Wildcards. Transfers and purchases must be done between competitors. (iv) The physical certificate must be surrendered for qualification. Photocopies and pictures are not valid. (v) Wildcards may be used at either World Championship show (Youth/Teen/Senior/Open) regardless of where the Wildcard was won or what is stated on the certificate. (vi) Competitors may use valid Wildcards awarded in their own name to enter World Championships using the show guidelines and deadlines for entry. Competitors wishing to use a valid transferred Wildcard must hold a membership current as of March 1st in the same year they wish to compete in the World Championship show.

docs.title: Membership is a privilege
docs.text: NBHA membership and participation in NBHA events is a privilege, not a right. Behavior which is damaging to the Association, or its membership will not be tolerated. Violation of any of the following provisions may subject a member to disqualification from NBHA events, being denied entry to NBHA events, loss of points, or suspension from the Association.

docs.title: Acts by family members
docs.text: Any act in connection with an NBHA sanctioned show or other NBHA business in violation of this section by a member of the family of an NBHA member may be deemed to have been committed by the NBHA member and subject him or her to penalties.

docs.title: Acts prejudicial to NBHA
docs.text: Any act deemed prejudicial to the best interests of the NBHA may result in the suspension of a member, including but not limited to the acts listed in F.2.a to F.2.i.

docs.title: Abusive language, threats, bribery, harassment
docs.text: Using abusive or intemperate language or attempting to threaten, bribe, influence or harass any contestant, show official or NBHA official. Also, any remarks made with the intent to cast aspersions on the character or integrity of an NBHA official or show official.

docs.title: Moving markers
docs.text: Moving or attempting to move markers at any time.

docs.title: Electronic or remote devices
docs.text: Use of electronic and/or remotely controlled devices to alter the outcome of a run.

docs.title: Horse abuse
docs.text: Abuse of a horse in any way, including but not limited to physical acts and neglect. NBHA Officials reserve the right to monitor stall management and the quality of well-being on any equine athlete at a sanctioned NBHA event.

docs.title: Competing impaired
docs.text: Competing while impaired and under the influence of drugs or alcohol.

docs.title: Misidentifying a horse
docs.text: Misidentifying a horse in any NBHA class will disqualify a contestant.

docs.title: Other conduct
docs.text: Other conduct that is not in the best interest of the NBHA or its members.

docs.title: Returned checks
docs.text: Failure to make good on a returned check to the NBHA or to any NBHA sanctioned event, or to any other association which has a cooperative agreement with the NBHA on returned checks.

docs.title: Dangerous horses
docs.text: Show Management and/or NBHA Directors at their sole discretion shall have the authority to disqualify or deny entry to any horse they deem dangerous to the rider, or to other individuals, animals, or property.

docs.title: Appeals
docs.text: A member who has been suspended, disqualified, or denied points under this section may appeal to an appeals committee of NBHA members and directors appointed by the appropriate State, Area, or Regional Director. The date, time, and location of such meeting will be determined by the State or Area Director. The decisions of such appeals committee shall be final and binding on all parties.

docs.title: Litigation
docs.text: Any litigation, whether pending or complete, including the NBHA, its directors, and/or any affiliated parties may result in further review by the NBHA on a case-by-case basis. NBHA reserves the right to suspend, refund or otherwise deny any membership or any relationship related to the NBHA as deemed necessary for the betterment and safety of the membership as a whole.

docs.title: Western attire requirements
docs.text: To enhance the image of our sport, the NBHA encourages and promotes appropriate western attire throughout all NBHA sanctioned events. Dress code is mandatory at State, National, Super and World Championship shows, unless otherwise stated. This includes a long-sleeved Western full button, full snapped or full zipped shirt with collar, jeans/pants and a western cowboy hat or helmet. Shirt sleeves must be rolled down and buttoned or snapped. Shirt tails must be tucked in. Jackets or coverings may be worn, but the western attire must exist regardless of cover. Western boots are highly recommended for safety. At all levels, including the district level, jeans/pants required.

docs.title: Dress code enforcement and fines
docs.text: This dress code will be strictly enforced at all State Championships, National Championship Series, the NBHA World Championships, the NBHA Youth World Championships, and all Super Shows, unless otherwise approved and stated for State Championship Shows. Anyone making a run at any of these shows that is found to be in violation of the dress code will be first given a verbal warning, and then assessed a $50 fine for any subsequent offense. A contestant cannot be disqualified for dress code offenses. During all Super Shows contestants will be assessed a fine of $10 for losing their hat at any time within the competition arena, however the fine will be $15 at World Shows, unless otherwise posted. Members who fail to pay such fines will be ineligible to compete in or enter any NBHA sanctioned or approved shows until such fines are paid in full. All disputes over dress code and fines will be decided by Show Management. The decision of Show Management will be final and binding.

docs.title: Closed-toe shoes and holding pens
docs.text: Anyone in any practice pen, holding area, or competition area must wear closed-toed shoes. When sufficiently posted, full western attire can be mandated in holding pens for all individuals, not just contestants.

docs.title: Written protests
docs.text: Persons who believe a rule violation or infraction has occurred at an NBHA event, may file a written protest with NBHA Headquarters by email. The protest must be made within 30 days of the incident which is being protested. NOTE: This rule does not prevent Directors and Show Managers from correcting obvious problems brought to their attention, without the submission of a written protest fee. Any situation not covered under these rules shall be decided by the NBHA official on site.

docs.title: Brand usage overview
docs.text: Overview of NBHA's intellectual property ('IP') rights and guidance on how the NBHA name and logos may be used. 'NBHA IP' means the logos, words and phrases, and other imagery to which NBHA holds exclusive rights. These guidelines are intended to provide guidance regarding the use of NBHA IP in any way that may reasonably be interpreted as implying endorsement, approval, sponsorship, or any other commercial affiliation by or with the NBHA. These guidelines are not intended to discourage the fair use of NBHA IP. NBHA retains the exclusive rights to its trademarks and copyrighted materials. NBHA allows access to NBHA IP solely for use in the promotion and marketing of NBHA and NBHA affiliated events.

docs.title: Logos
docs.text: The NBHA owns and has the right to control logos (in full or part) in the United States and Canada and within its internationally affiliated associations, including the official logo graphics and the trademarked words and phrases below the logo. Font of NBHA logo: Basel Neue Black Italic and Athelas. Red: C 0 / M 97 / Y 80 / K 20. Blue: C 100 / M 94 / Y 0 / K 35. Official logos exist with and without the horse and rider. At no time can the logo be disassembled or rearranged beyond the official versions.

docs.title: Words and phrases
docs.text: The NBHA has exclusive right to, but not limited to: NATIONAL BARREL HORSE ASSOCIATION; NBHA.

docs.title: Photographs
docs.text: The NBHA has the right to control the commercial use of photographs or other images from NBHA events. A competitor's entry provides consent for their image to be used for NBHA promotional purposes across digital or print platforms. NBHA reserves exclusive rights to all photography privileges at sanctioned events. Any photography on-site or use of media whether for personal or commercial use must obtain prior approval from the NBHA office.

docs.title: Commercial use in the US and Canada
docs.text: No United States or Canada business or other commercial entity should use NBHA IP without the express consent of the NBHA.

docs.title: International sponsors
docs.text: International sponsors, who sponsor an NBHA association in a country besides the United States or Canada, can use the NBHA logo from their country but it must not be used as a stand-alone logo. The NBHA country (i.e., NBHA AUSTRALIA) MUST be placed alongside the NBHA Official logo, and additions to the logo must not interfere, modify, or overlap the Official NBHA logo.

docs.title: State and District guidelines (US and Canada)
docs.text: Official affiliated NBHA districts are bound by the following guidelines. Failing to follow NBHA IP guidelines may jeopardize official affiliation with NBHA. Districts MUST use the Official NBHA logo in conjunction with the District name (ie. NBHA TX 15). States and Districts are NOT permitted to use any NBHA IP as a stand-alone logo.

docs.title: District award guidelines and trophy buckles
docs.text: (a) An official affiliated NBHA District is permitted to use the Official NBHA logo on awards items presented at single races or for year-end awards, that include but are not limited to clothing, embroidery, trophy tack, trophies. (b) An official affiliated NBHA District is NOT permitted to use the Official NBHA logo on any trophy belt buckle. Gist Silversmiths maintains exclusive right to the use of the NBHA logo within the United States and Canada. (c) An official affiliated NBHA District may use the letters NBHA (in a generic font) on a trophy belt buckle, but the full NBHA logo (with or without the horse and rider image attached) is reserved for exclusive use by the Official NBHA Silversmith, Gist Silversmiths. Districts are encouraged to order trophy buckles, with the NBHA logo, from Gist Silversmiths.

docs.title: District marketing guidelines
docs.text: NBHA Districts are permitted to use NBHA IP on marketing materials, that include websites, social media posts, printed flyers, and barrel covers. The NBHA District number (i.e., NBHA TX 15) MUST be placed alongside the NBHA Official logo. Additions to the logo must not interfere, modify, or overlap the Official NBHA logo.

docs.title: District merchandise guidelines
docs.text: (a) An official NBHA affiliated District is permitted to use the NBHA logo on Official District merchandise that is available for sale to the public or awarded to District members. Districts MUST use the Official NBHA logo in conjunction with the District name (ie. NBHA TX 15). (b) Districts are NOT permitted to use any NBHA IP as a stand-alone logo. All merchandise items produced by Districts, for in-District use, must contain the District name, alongside the Official NBHA logo (ie. NBHA TX 15).

docs.title: Global guidelines (outside US and Canada)
docs.text: Official internationally affiliated NBHA associations are bound by the following guidelines. Failing to follow NBHA IP guidelines may jeopardize official affiliation with NBHA. The NBHA country (i.e., NBHA AUSTRALIA) MUST be placed alongside the NBHA Official logo, and additions to the logo must not interfere, modify, or overlap the Official NBHA logo (e.g., NBHA ITALY).

docs.title: International award guidelines
docs.text: (a) An official affiliated NBHA International association is permitted to use the full NBHA logo on awards items presented at single races or for year-end awards. The NBHA country (e.g., NBHA ITALY) MUST be placed alongside the NBHA Official logo, and additions to the logo must not interfere, modify, or overlap the Official NBHA logo. (b) The promotion of international awards featuring the letters NBHA or the full NBHA logo MUST be limited to digital and print platforms based in their country of origin.

docs.title: International marketing guidelines
docs.text: (a) International NBHA affiliated associations are permitted to use NBHA IP on event marketing materials, that include websites, social media posts, printed flyers, and barrel covers. The NBHA country (i.e., NBHA ITALY) MUST be placed alongside the NBHA Official logo, and additions to the logo must not interfere, modify, or overlap the Official NBHA logo. (b) Digital and printed promotions of sponsors of internationally affiliated NBHA associations MUST be limited to digital and print platforms owned in their home country (e.g., NBHA Australia sponsors cannot be promoted on a United States based webpage, platform, or social media page).

docs.title: International merchandise guidelines
docs.text: (a) International NBHA affiliated associations are permitted to use the NBHA logo on merchandise that is available for sale to the public or awarded to international members. International NBHA affiliated associations MUST use the Official NBHA logo in conjunction with their country name (e.g., NBHA ITALY). (b) International NBHA affiliated associations are NOT permitted to use any NBHA IP as a stand-alone logo. All merchandise items produced by international NBHA affiliated associations, for international use, must contain the country name, alongside the Official NBHA logo.

docs.title: Social media
docs.text: The NBHA recognizes that the nature of social media encourages people to talk about current events and topics; and NBHA appreciates the interest, excitement, and public conversation surrounding NBHA events, but only Official NBHA Districts, State Directors, and affiliated international associations have permission to use NBHA IP in social media. This section applies to all social media platforms including but not limited to Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Snapchat, Google+ and others.

docs.title: Protecting NBHA IP
docs.text: NBHA is committed to protect the NBHA's rights. These guidelines are not intended to provide legal advice and any information contained herein does not in any way limit the NBHA's legal rights and remedies. NBHA rules and regulations protecting NBHA IP regarding logo usage are applicable to State and District Directors and apply to members and non-members on an individual level. An NBHA member or non-member is subject to the same rules as State and District Directors and may not use the NBHA logo or an NBHA Tour Event Logo on a standalone basis.

docs.title: No Time
docs.text: A run that receives no recorded time. Given for going off pattern, knocking over a barrel completely, running out of turn or on a horse other than the drawn horse, or falling off after crossing the starting timer (A.8). Also given for any penalty during a rerun (A.16) and for lead line in Super Show and Championship classes (E.2.c, E.3.e).

docs.title: Division (1D to 5D)
docs.text: A time bracket within a class, set from the fastest time. 1D is the fastest time; 2D starts at fastest plus 0.5 seconds; 3D at plus 1 second; 4D at plus 1.5 seconds; 5D at plus 2 seconds and is open-ended (C.4).

docs.title: 3D, 4D and 5D Format
docs.text: The number of divisions a show pays out on. 3D uses 1.0 second splits; 4D uses 0.5-0.5-0.5 or 0.5-0.5-1 second splits; 5D uses 0.5 second splits. Points are always awarded in 5D regardless of payout format (B.2, D.3).

docs.title: Draw
docs.text: The randomly determined running order for a class. Once set it may only be changed to separate entries with the same horse, rider or immediate family, with changes moved to the end (A.13).

docs.title: Drag
docs.text: Reworking and leveling the ground around the barrels with a ground tool pulled by a motor vehicle, required after no more than every 5 contestants at a consistent interval (A.5).

docs.title: Rerun
docs.text: A repeat run granted when the timers fail or barrels are not properly on their markers. Penalties from the original run are not carried over, but any penalty on the rerun results in a no time (A.16).

docs.title: Rollover / Carryover
docs.text: Using one run's time in more than one class on the same day with identical pattern and arena/drag specifics. Must be declared before the event (or before the rider's draw position if so stated) and both entry fees paid (B.8.a).

docs.title: Roving District (00)
docs.text: An optional state-level district whose members may earn points at any show sanctioned for any district in their state, counting up to ten shows per class. Time splits are taken from the fastest time in the class (C.16).

docs.title: Immediate family
docs.text: Husband, wife, siblings, children and grandchildren residing in the same household, including children and grandchildren at school away from home who reside part of the year with their parents or grandparents (A.11.a).

docs.title: Altered pattern
docs.text: A change to the pattern that cannot be restored, including changes in the staked barrel positions, the timing device position (vertically or horizontally), or the entry gate position. Runs made before the alteration are void for points unless the whole class is rerun (A.9).

docs.title: Office charge
docs.text: The portion of entry fees a show may withhold from the jackpot: a maximum of 25%, or 30% if at least $1,000 is added (D.1).

docs.title: Non-member permit fee
docs.text: A fee of up to $10 per show paid by non-members to compete for prize money at an NBHA sanctioned show, deposited in the district year-end awards account (B.15).

docs.title: Member in good standing
docs.text: A current NBHA member. Required to earn points. A 30-day administrative grace period applies after expiry, but members in the grace period are not credited points unless they renew online before competing (C.1).

docs.title: Co-sanctioned show
docs.text: A show sanctioned by more than one district, each paying the $30 fee and submitting its own form. Each district's members receive points separately based on their own district's fastest time (B.12, C.4, C.11).

docs.title: Wildcard
docs.text: A physical certificate good for one horse qualification into one World Championship class. Does not expire, is transferable with a transfer form, and cannot be replaced if lost (E.3.k).

docs.title: Lead line
docs.text: A rider led through the pattern. Lead line competitors never receive points toward World Championship qualifications, and lead line in a Super Show or Championship class results in a no-time (C.3, E.2.c, E.3.e).

docs.title: Three-call
docs.text: At Super and World Shows, a rider who fails to check in during the drag is called three times and misses the run if unable to enter the arena during those calls (E.2.h, E.3.f).

docs.title: Run-off
docs.text: A tiebreaker run for 1st place in a division at State or World Championships, with at least 30 minutes rest and a 5 second penalty per barrel knocked down. Prize money is still split and riders are Co-Champions (E.1.k, E.3.i).
